metric_identity.metric_name: AI in Enterprise Software (SaaS+AI Adoption, Copilot Attach Rates, Productivity Gains)
metric_identity.source_report: Menlo Ventures 2025 State of Generative AI in the Enterprise; Gartner GenAI Spending Forecast (March 2025); Mordor Intelligence Enterprise AI Market Report; Microsoft FY2026 Earnings; GitHub Copilot Usage Reports
metric_identity.methodology_notes: Menlo Ventures surveyed 600 enterprise IT decision-makers and analyzed vendor revenue data to track enterprise generative AI spending from $1.7B (2023) to $37B (2025). Gartner's forecast covers worldwide GenAI spending across infrastructure, software, and services. Mordor Intelligence uses primary and secondary research for enterprise AI market sizing ($97.2B in 2025). Microsoft Copilot metrics are drawn from quarterly earnings calls (15M paid seats as of January 2026). GitHub Copilot data from Microsoft disclosures and third-party analyses. Productivity gain figures from GitHub's controlled study of 4,800 developers and McKinsey Global Survey on AI 2025. IDC and Gartner agent adoption forecasts based on vendor roadmap analysis and enterprise surveys. Copilot attach rates computed from Microsoft's disclosed 8M active M365 Copilot users against 440M total M365 subscribers (1.81%). Multiple sources cross-referenced for convergence.

metric_value.value: $37 billion enterprise generative AI spending in 2025 (3.2x YoY); $97.2 billion enterprise AI market (2025); $644 billion worldwide GenAI spending (2025); Microsoft 365 Copilot: 15 million paid seats, 1.81% attach rate across 440M subscribers; GitHub Copilot: 20 million cumulative users, 1.3 million paid subscribers, 42% market share of AI coding tools ($7.37B market); AI copilots generate 46% of code on average; developer task completion 55% faster with Copilot
metric_value.comparison_baseline: Enterprise generative AI spending was $11.5B in 2024 and $1.7B in 2023. Microsoft 365 Copilot had 4.7M paid subscribers in Q1 FY2026, growing 75% YoY. GitHub Copilot had 1.3M paid subscribers in Q1 2025, growing 30% QoQ. Traditional SaaS deal conversion rates average 25%, versus 47% for AI deals. In 2024, 47% of enterprise AI solutions were built internally vs. 53% purchased; by 2025 this shifted to 24% built vs. 76% purchased. Only 6% of enterprises had moved GenAI beyond pilot into production (Gartner 2025).
metric_value.market_layer: application (AI copilots and SaaS+AI products sit at the application layer, built on top of foundation models and cloud infrastructure, delivered as enterprise software)

trend.year_over_year_change: +221% YoY in enterprise GenAI spending ($11.5B to $37B, 2024 to 2025); +76.4% worldwide GenAI spending growth (Gartner, 2025); GitHub revenue +40% YoY driven by Copilot; Microsoft 365 Copilot paid subscribers +75% YoY; 50+ AI products now exceed $100M ARR, at least 10 exceed $1B ARR
trend.compound_annual_growth_rate: Enterprise AI market: 18.9% CAGR (2025-2030) per Mordor Intelligence ($97.2B to $229.3B); broader estimates range from 19-49% CAGR depending on scope definition; Gartner AI software market: 19.1% CAGR with growth accelerating from 17.8% to 20.4% by 2027; AI assistant market: 44.5% CAGR (2025-2030) per MarketsandMarkets ($3.35B to $21.11B)
trend.forecast_value: $229.3 billion enterprise AI market by 2030 (Mordor Intelligence); $21.11 billion AI assistant market by 2030 (MarketsandMarkets); 40% of enterprise apps will feature AI agents by 2026 (Gartner, up from <5% in 2025); 80% of enterprise workplace apps will embed AI copilots by 2026 (IDC)
trend.velocity_indicator: Enterprise GenAI spending grew from $1.7B to $37B in just 2 years (22x, 2023-2025), the fastest enterprise software category expansion in history. AI deals convert at 47% vs. 25% for traditional SaaS (nearly 2x). Gartner projects AI agent penetration in enterprise apps jumping from <5% to 40% within a single year (2025-2026). At least 10 AI products crossed $1B ARR within 2-3 years of launch. GitHub Copilot grew from 0 to 20M users and $2B+ run rate in under 3 years.

entrepreneurial_relevance.relevance_for_entrepreneurs: The AI-in-enterprise-software sector represents the most important market context for any startup founder building B2B products today. Three critical dynamics define this market: (1) The SaaS+AI spending explosion ($37B in 2025, up 22x from 2023) creates a massive opportunity for startups that embed AI into vertical workflows. Menlo Ventures data shows startups capture $2 for every $1 incumbents earn in enterprise AI, meaning agile newcomers currently have a structural advantage. (2) The copilot attach rate paradox is instructive: Microsoft 365 Copilot has only a 1.81% attach rate despite being bundled with the world's most ubiquitous enterprise software, while GitHub Copilot achieved 90% Fortune 100 adoption. This reveals that AI products succeed when they deliver clear, measurable productivity gains in specific workflows (55% faster developer task completion) rather than vague general-purpose augmentation. Founders should target specific, measurable pain points. (3) The pilot-to-production gap is real: only 6% of enterprises have moved GenAI beyond pilots (Gartner), and 70-85% of AI initiatives fail to meet expected outcomes. This means the winners will be startups that solve the 'last mile' of AI deployment — integration, reliability, compliance, and measurable ROI. The application layer captures the majority of enterprise AI spending ($19B of $37B in 2025), confirming that the value in AI is shifting from model providers to product builders. For French/European founders, GDPR compliance and data sovereignty requirements create a defensible niche against US hyperscalers.
entrepreneurial_relevance.actionable_insight: Build vertical AI copilots with embedded, measurable productivity metrics rather than horizontal platforms. The 47% AI deal conversion rate (vs. 25% for traditional SaaS) and the $2-to-$1 startup advantage over incumbents mean the window is open now but closing. Focus on the pilot-to-production gap: enterprises are desperate for AI tools that actually work in production, not just impressive demos. Price on value delivered (productivity gains, cost savings) rather than per-seat, since Microsoft's low attach rate shows per-seat pricing faces resistance at $30/month/user.

confidence.cross_reference: Enterprise AI spending figures triangulated across Menlo Ventures ($37B), Gartner ($644B total GenAI spend), and Mordor Intelligence ($97.2B enterprise AI market). Microsoft Copilot data from official earnings calls (15M paid seats, January 2026) cross-referenced with Business of Apps and Lighthouse Global analyses. GitHub Copilot metrics from Microsoft earnings, TechCrunch reporting, and GitHub's own research publications. Productivity gains confirmed by GitHub's 4,800-developer controlled study (55% faster task completion) and McKinsey Global Survey (26-55% gains). Gartner and IDC agent/copilot penetration forecasts independently converge on rapid 2026 enterprise adoption. The pilot-to-production gap (6% beyond pilot) is corroborated by both Gartner and MIT studies. Bubble risk indicators supported by the $400B capex vs. $100B revenue disconnect and MIT finding that 95% of GenAI pilots fail to achieve business value.
confidence.caveats: The wide range of CAGR estimates (18.9% to 49%) reflects different market scope definitions across research firms. Menlo Ventures is a VC firm with investment interests in enterprise AI, creating potential bias toward optimistic framing. Microsoft's copilot subscriber counts include both active and inactive seats. The 1.81% attach rate may undercount adoption since many enterprises are in phased rollouts and pilot stages. Productivity gain metrics (55% faster, 46% code generation) are measured in controlled conditions and may not reflect real-world enterprise environments. The 70-85% AI initiative failure rate and the 95% pilot failure rate (MIT) create significant tension with the bullish spending growth figures, suggesting either over-investment or measurement lag. Enterprise AI spending conflates genuine production deployments with pilot spending and shelfware. Per-vendor revenue disclosures remain limited, making cross-verification difficult for some claims.
